identity.title: Cosmo-tomography toward PKS 1830‒211: Variability of the quasar and of its foreground molecular absorption monitored with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We used ALMA to monitor the submillimeter continuum emission of PKS 1830$-$211, together with the absorption spectra of the H$_2$O and CH molecules, with 17 visits spread over six months in 2016.
Complementing this, we used available ALMA data to investigate changes in the system in the period 2012-2022.

evidence.quote: PKS 1830$-$211 is a blazar at $z=2.5$ (cite: lid99) with strong gravitational lensing due to an intervening nearly face-on spiral galaxy at $z=0.89$ (cite: wik96; win02).
Sky frequencies are calculated for $z$=0.88582.
PKS 1830$-$211 is a blazar at $z=2.5$ (cite: lid99) with strong gravitational lensing due to an intervening nearly face-on spiral galaxy at $z=0.89$ (cite: wik96; win02).
Sky frequencies are calculated for $z$=0.88582.

question.value: How do the submillimeter continuum emission and foreground molecular absorption of the lensed quasar PKS 1830-211 vary over time, and what constraints do these variations place on the quasar's activity and small-scale ISM structures in the z=0.89 absorber?

evidence.quote: We aim to study the time variations of the system (the two main lensed images of the quasar and the two corresponding sightlines in the absorber) in order to obtain constraints on both the quasar activity and small-scale structures in the interstellar medium of the absorber.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00405.S (observations of H$_2$O and CH in April 2012)
ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00056.S (observations of H$_2$O and CH in May 2014)
ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00020.S (observations of H$_2$O, CH, H$_2^{18}$O, and H$_2^{17}$O in July 2014)
ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00075.S (2016 monitoring of H$_2$O and CH)
ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00051.S (observations of H$_2^{18}$O in 2019)
ADS/JAO.ALMA#2021.A.00028.S (observations of H$_2^{18}$O and H$_2^{17}$O in 2022).

The correlator setup was chosen to simultaneously cover the ground-state transitions of H$_2$O (557 GHz, rest frequency) and CH (two $\Lambda$-doublets at $\sim 533$ and 537 GHz, rest frequency) redshifted into Band 7.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 3 spectral windows at ~282.4, 284.6, 295.4 GHz (938 MHz bandwidth, 0.56 MHz / 0.6 km/s resolution after Hanning smoothing); 1 continuum window at 296.8 GHz (31.25 MHz resolution)

evidence.quote: To cover these lines, three spectral windows were centered at $\sim$282.4, 284.6, and 295.4 GHz sky frequency, with a bandwidth of 938 MHz and a spectral resolution of 0.56 MHz, resulting in a velocity resolution of 0.6 km s$^{-1}$ after Hanning smoothing.
A fourth spectral window, not including any detectable spectral line, was centered at 296.8 GHz with a coarser spectral resolution of 31.25 MHz in order to provide extra continuum data.
We targeted the fundamental ground-state transitions of ortho-H$_2$O and CH (two $\Lambda$-doublets J=3/2–1/2), which can be observed simultaneously in one ALMA tuning in band 7.
Here, we present the first detection of $^{13}$CH toward the SW image of PKS 1830$-$211 in the average spectra of the 2016 monitoring data.

The on-source integration time for each visit was slightly less than 10 min, set by our original goal, which is to be able to track changes in the spectral line profiles down to a few percent during each individual visit.

findings_qualitative.value: PCA of the absorption spectra reveals wavy variations with a ~230-day period across both sightlines and species, potentially tied to the helical jet precession of the quasar.

evidence.quote: A principal component analysis of the absorption spectra toward both images of PKS 1830$-$211 reveals a seemingly wavy behavior of the variations during the monitoring, with an apparent period of $\sim 230$ days, although this timescale is longer than the time span of our survey and would therefore need to be confirmed with a longer monitoring.

findings_qualitative.value: A continuous, shallow (tau < 0.01) water absorption trough spanning nearly 500 km/s is detected toward the SW sightline, suggesting extra-planar or circumgalactic molecular gas.

evidence.loc: Weak and broad water absorption trough in the SW sightline
evidence.quote: In addition, the ALMA “super” spectrum of the H$_2$O absorption now reveals an even more surprising structure in the form of a weak ($\tau < 0.01$) continuous absorption trough covering a wide velocity range of nearly 500 km s$^{-1}$ toward the SW image (Fig. 15c).

findings_qualitative.value: The H2O/CH optical depth ratio in the z=0.89 absorber is comparable to that in Milky Way translucent clouds, with higher H2O/CH toward SW than NE, similar to the Galactic CMZ vs disk trend.

evidence.quote: Moreover, the differences in H$_2$O and CH$^*$ opacity ratios between the SW and NE lines of sight follow a similar trend to that observed in the Milky Way between clouds in the central molecular zone (CMZ) and the Galactic disk

claims.hypothesis: A simple parametric model of a stable optically thick core plus a single adiabatically expanding ballistic plasmon can explain both the 80% flux decay and the systematic spectral-index difference between the NE and SW lensed images, while constraining the lensing time delay and differential magnification.
claims.experiment: Fit the 7-parameter core+plasmon model via MCMC simultaneously to the NE and SW flux densities, NE spectral index, and spectral-index difference across the 17 monitoring epochs.
claims.result: The model reproduces the light-curve decay and spectral-index difference, yielding a time delay of 25 +/- 3 days and differential magnification of 1.24 +/- 0.04, consistent with the Von Neumann randomness valley.
claims.finding: A single cooling plasmon plus stable core accounts for the continuum and polarization evolution and yields a lensing time delay consistent with lens models, though the delay value is model- and weight-dependent.

evidence.loc: Simple scenario of the continuum evolution
evidence.quote: Even though the model is not able to reproduce the scatter seen in spectral index, it is remarkable that such a simple model can capture the light-curve decrease and the (overall) spectral differences between the NE and SW images in a consistent way.

evidence.loc: Simple scenario of the continuum evolution
evidence.quote: Still, the best fit value of $\Delta t = 25 \pm 3$ days is consistent with lensing models (cite: mul20b).

claims.hypothesis: Time variations in the foreground molecular absorption profiles are driven by periodic changes in background illumination from a precessing helical jet in the quasar.
claims.experiment: Perform Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on the 2016 monitoring spectra of H2O and CH toward both SW and NE images and fit sine functions to the first principal component eigenvalues.
claims.result: PC1 eigenvalues across independent velocity ranges, species (H2O, CH), and sightlines (SW, NE) show sinusoidal variations with a consistent period of ~230 days.
claims.finding: The wavy absorption variations likely originate from background continuum illumination modulated by the quasar's helical jet, though confirmation requires monitoring over a timespan longer than the ~230-day period.

evidence.quote: All these measurements (Table 1; except overlapping velocity range for measurements from H$_2$O spectra) are independent, but still yield a consistent signal period of $\sim 230$ days for PC1, within error bars.

This interpretation would indeed bring a natural explanation for the time variability of the absorption lines toward PKS 1830$-$211, but would need to be tested with new monitoring data over a longer time span.

claims.hypothesis: The elemental 12C/13C and oxygen isotopic ratios in the z=0.89 absorber reflect a less nucleosynthetically processed ISM compared to the local Milky Way, while other carbon-bearing species suffer from chemical fractionation.
claims.experiment: Stack all 17 monitoring spectra to detect 13CH and simultaneously fit multi-Gaussian hyperfine profiles to 12CH and 13CH; similarly fit H2(16)O, H2(18)O, and H2(17)O in 2014 and 2022 spectra.
claims.result: Measured 12CH/13CH = 150 +/- 10 (higher than CH+, CH3OH, HCO+, HCN, HNC along the same sightline), 16O/18O = 65.3 +/- 0.7, and 18O/17O = 11.5 +/- 0.5.
claims.finding: CH and H2O isotopologs provide unfractionated isotopic ratios indicating a less processed ISM dominated by massive-star nucleosynthesis at z=0.89, whereas other C-bearing molecules are affected by fractionation.

evidence.quote: Compared to the $^{12}$C-/$^{13}$C- isotopolog ratios from other species in the SW line of sight toward PKS 1830$-$211, the $^{12}$CH/$^{13}$CH ratio is the highest measured so far: $97 \pm 6$ for $^{12}$CH$^+$/$^{13}$CH$^+$ (cite: mul17), $62 \pm 3$ for CH$_3$OH/$^{13}$CH$_3$OH (cite: mul21), and even lower values $20-50$ for HCO$^+$, HCN, and HNC (cite: mul06; mul11). This strongly suggests that all these other species may be affected by fractionation issues.

evidence.loc: Water isotopologs and oxygen isotopic ratios
evidence.quote: Regarding the $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio discussed above (Sect. 4.4.1), the oxygen isotopic ratios point to a different ISM isotopic composition from that of the solar neighborhood in the Milky Way today (e.g., (cite: luc98)), namely one that is less processed and most likely dominated by massive-star nucleosynthesis

why_this_data.value: PKS 1830-211 has high submm brightness, superluminal jet motions, lens magnification, and rich foreground molecular absorption; Band 7 simultaneously covers saturated ortho-H2O (probing line wings and optically thin NE sightline) and optically thin CH (tau ~ 1, probing SW line center) with <0.5'' resolution to separate the 1'' lensed images.

evidence.quote: During the monitoring, the array configuration changed, but the longest baseline was always longer than 450 m, such that the synthesized beam was always smaller than 0.5$\ensuremath{''}$ and the two main lensed images of the quasar are therefore always well resolved.

The H$_2$O absorption is deeply saturated toward the SW image near $v \sim 0$ km s$^{-1}$ (cite: mul14), but its large opacity is well suited to investigating the variations of the line wings. The H$_2$O line is also well suited to probing changes in the presumably optically thin NE absorption. On the other hand, the CH absorption reaches an apparent peak opacity of $\tau \sim 1$ along the SW line of sight, complementing the H$_2$O line in tracing variations in the line center of the SW absorption.

why_this_method.value: Fitting visibilities directly with UVMultiFit and taking relative ratios (flux ratio R, double polarization ratio R_pol, spectral index difference Delta alpha) removes instrumental and absolute flux calibration systematics; PCA isolates coherent multi-channel spectral variations.

evidence.quote: In addition, while the absolute flux accuracy is of $\sim 10\%-20$%, we emphasize that the accuracy of relative quantities, such as the flux-density ratio of both lensed images and the polarization ratio, is much higher (e.g., at a per mil level for the flux density ratio), and can therefore offer subtle diagnostics of the quasar activity, as discussed in the following subsections.
To extract more information from the variations of the absorption line profile, we ran a principal component analysis (PCA).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Micro-lensing or intrinsic absorber cloud motions/chemistry as the primary cause of the 2016 short-term absorption variations — rejected in favor of intrinsic quasar continuum morphology changes because ISM dynamical/chemical timescales are too long and variations are coherent across both sightlines during an 80% intrinsic flux drop.

evidence.loc: Analysis of the absorption profiles and their time variations
evidence.quote: To further characterize the absorption variations, we can assume that the absorbing screen is constant in time, that is, $d\tau(x,y)/dt =0$. This is justified by the fact that the timescales associated with potential causes of variations in the absorber are much longer than those we are interested in, even for small-scale structures on AU- to pc scales.

evidence.loc: Possible causes of time variations of the continuum distribution
evidence.quote: Given the quasi-monotonic and severe decrease in the flux density of PKS 1830$-$211 during our six-month monitoring (by $\sim 80$% ), the short (timescale of the order of one week) and regular variations of the absorption spectra, and the apparent coherence (periodicity?) of the variations over $\gtrsim 200$ days seen toward both lensed images, we conclude that they are most likely due to intrinsic changes in the background continuum distribution, that is, the activity of the quasar, rather than to micro-lensing events.

how_they_decided_enough.value: 10 min on-source per visit was chosen to reach <1% continuum rms to track percent-level line variations; Gaussian components were added to CH and water isotopolog fits until residuals/reduced chi-squared stabilized.

evidence.quote: The on-source integration time for each visit was slightly less than 10 min, set by our original goal, which is to be able to track changes in the spectral line profiles down to a few percent during each individual visit.
During the process, we found that the ratio was relatively stable around approximately $150$, while the uncertainties and fit residuals decrease with an increasing number of velocity components.

limitations_admitted.value: The nearly monotonic, featureless light curve in 2016 causes a strong degeneracy between time delay and differential magnification in the Von Neumann analysis.

evidence.loc: The time delay and the differential magnification factor
evidence.quote: Given the quasi-monotonic and relatively featureless light curve of PKS 1830$-$211 during our monitoring, there is a strong degeneracy between the two parameters.

limitations_admitted.value: The time delay constraint from the parametric continuum model is highly model-dependent and sensitive to the relative weighting of flux densities and spectral indices.

evidence.loc: Simple scenario of the continuum evolution
evidence.quote: The constraint on the time delay, $\Delta t$, is highly model dependent

limitations_admitted.value: Limited parallactic angle coverage and Dual-Pol (XX, YY) observations prevent quantitative constraints on the core and plasmon EVPAs.

evidence.quote: we notice that the parallactic angle coverage of our data is very limited, which prevents us from putting robust constraints on the core and plasmon EVPAs.

limitations_admitted.value: The ~230-day period found by PCA is comparable to the 6-month monitoring duration and requires longer monitoring to confirm true periodicity.

evidence.quote: These periods are comparable to the duration of our monitoring and it remains to be seen if the evolution is truly periodic with monitoring over longer timescales.

limitations_admitted.value: Mass of the gas producing the 500 km/s water absorption trough cannot be meaningfully estimated due to unknown spatial distribution.

evidence.loc: Weak and broad water absorption trough in the SW sightline
evidence.quote: Given the lack of constraints on the distribution of such material in the halo (probably fragmented in filamentary structures), it is not possible to get a meaningful estimate of its mass content.

referee_caveats_inferred: Fitting a sinusoid to PCA eigenvalues over a 187-day baseline to claim a ~230-272 day period is susceptible to red-noise / random-walk drift producing apparent half-or-single-cycle waves.
The parametric time delay (25 +/- 3 days) relies entirely on the assumed functional form of adiabatic plasmon decay to break the strong light-curve degeneracy.

evidence.quote: In addition to the 2016 monitoring data, we also used observations of PKS 1830$-$211 available in the ALMA archive to extract continuum information (flux density and flux density ratio) between 2012 and 2022

This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00405.S (observations of H$_2$O and CH in April 2012), ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00056.S (observations of H$_2$O and CH in May 2014), ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00020.S (observations of H$_2$O, CH, H$_2^{18}$O, and H$_2^{17}$O in July 2014), ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00075.S (2016 monitoring of H$_2$O and CH), ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00051.S (observations of H$_2^{18}$O in 2019), ADS/JAO.ALMA#2021.A.00028.S (observations of H$_2^{18}$O and H$_2^{17}$O in 2022).
